hook_text: Stop guessing your quadratic roots. Do this instead.
clip_script: The zero-product property states a simple but absolute truth: if the product of two or more quantities equals zero, then at least one of those quantities must be equal to zero. If I tell you that A multiplied by B equals zero, logic dictates that either A equals zero, B equals zero, or both equal zero. There is no other way to multiply two numbers and arrive at zero. We apply this property directly to our factored equation. We have the quantity x plus one, multiplied by the quantity two x plus three, set equal to zero. According to the zero-product property, either the first factor equals zero, or the second factor equals zero.
